subject: Renewal negotiation — Tidewater Energy (exec approval request)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@tidewater-energy.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2029 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal — Tidewater Energy

Marissa,

Thanks for sending the renewal; we reviewed the numbers with finance and procurement. Given the usage drop in Q3 (attached) and a consolidation of our vendor spend, the renewal as-is exceeds our approved budget. We understand Redwood’s value, but we need concessions to move forward. Specifically: 

- A material price reduction for year 1 (we're targeting ~25-30% off the proposed ARR)
- A 60-day term reset / alignment to our fiscal calendar so the majority of consumption falls into our budgeted period
- A credit for the recent outage window (we incurred incremental cloud spend) and an SLA addendum for 99.95%

We’re ready to commit to an 18-month renewal if we can reach agreement on concession structure. We need clarity by COB Friday to include this in our Q4 planning.

I’ve attached our Q3 usage export and a marked-up copy of the contract redlines. Happy to discuss live.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Procurement
Tidewater Energy

Attachments: tidewater_usage_q3.csv (csv), tidewater_redlines.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2029 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal proposal — Tidewater Energy — exec approval request

Team — forwarding Tidewater's ask. TL;DR: they want an aggressive price reduction (25-30% target), 60-day term reset, and an SLA credit for a recent outage. They’ve signaled willingness for an 18-month commitment if we concede.

Quick context:
- Current ARR: $1,200,000 per year (standard commercial renewal)
- Q3 usage down ~22% vs. year ago; their FY24 forecast is spotty but committed to cloud-heavy projects in H2
- Risk: if we won’t move, they’ll evaluate a different provider and likely reduce scope to embeddings-only

My suggested paths for approval:
A) Commercial compromise (fast, preserves margin): 15% one-time discount off year-one ARR + 3-month consumption credit (applied over first invoice) + $20k SLA credit. Keep renewal length at 12 months, no term reset.
B) Executive concession (bigger win but higher cost): 18% discount year one + 60-day term reset + $35k SLA credit, conditional on 18-month lock and a usage baseline in SOW.

I prefer B if leadership will authorize — it buys the 18-month commitment they want and reduces churn risk. Asking for exec signoff or an alternative direction by EOD tomorrow so I can reply to procurement before their Friday deadline. Attachments from customer included.

- Marissa
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoood.com

Attachments referenced: tidewater_usage_q3.csv, tidewater_redlines.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2029 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal — Tidewater Energy — exec approval request

Marissa — thanks for the summary. A few quick thoughts from a margins/precedent POV: 

- 25-30% entrenches a tough precedent for the region; we should avoid a straight % discount if we can (it’s visible in benchmarks).
- Prefer one-time usage credit rather than pushing a durable %-off list price. A $50k one-time credit against year-one invoices would be meaningful to them while preserving list price integrity.
- Term reset: I’m okay with a short alignment but not a full 60-day reset that effectively extends their invoicing cycle without additional commitment. If they insist on alignment, tie it to an 18-month committed ARR with an early-termination repayment clause.

Please run the math on option B vs my suggested hybrid (12% discount + $50k credit + SLA credit $25k). I'll loop in Finance if the final approval leans toward the larger concession.

-Ben
VP, Sales Operations
ben_carter@redwoood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Oct 2029 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal — Tidewater Energy — exec approval request

Team — I reviewed the situation and the proposed options. The most important objective is to retain Tidewater given their strategic footprint (energy vertical, potential channel work). I’m authorizing a controlled concession with conditions: 

Approval (final):
- 18% one-time discount applied to year-one ARR (not a list-price change)
- $35,000 SLA credit to cover recent outage impact, posted as a one-time invoice credit
- 90-day term reset (not 60) to align their billing start — we will not extend the overall committed term; the renewal duration remains 18 months as they requested, with the new start date moved 90 days forward.

Conditions:
1) Tidewater signs the attached SOW amendment that defines a 12-month usage baseline and commits to an 18-month auto-renewal after the initial 18-month term.
2) Include an early termination clause requiring repayment of the discount/credit on a prorated basis if they terminate before the 18 months.
3) Finance will validate the ARR impact; Marissa, work with Priyom to document the margin and post-approval operational steps.

Marissa — please send the counter with these exact terms and include the SOW draft. If Tidewater accepts, mark deal DW-8931 as "Saved — Exec Concession" and route for billing adjustments.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales — North America
laura_bennett@redwoood.com

(Attachment: approval_summary_for_fulfillment.pdf)
